Let me think this through as I plan for the year.

My 70 mu is mostly wheat-maize like everyone around here in Quzhou. That's what I know best. I'll put most of the land — 50 mu — in wheat-maize rotation. The other 20 mu I split among the cash crops: cotton 8 mu (cotton prices are okay and I have the experience now after 6 years), watermelon 5 mu, cauliflower 4 mu, chili 3 mu. Vegetables make more money per mu but they take a lot of work and my household only has 3 people, so I can't grow too much.

For wheat I'll use the Jimai improved variety like last year. I put about 50 jin of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base before sowing, then top dress with urea around jointing — maybe 30 jin urea. That works out to roughly 25-26 kg N. My neighbor old Wang got 480 kg/mu last year doing similar, so I aim for 500. I irrigate 3 times: winter water, jointing, and grain-fill. Spray for aphids and powdery mildew, usually 2 times.

Maize comes right after wheat harvest in June. I use Zhengdan hybrid seed. Less fertilizer than wheat because the wheat residue gives something back — about 18 kg N base plus a top-dress at big-trumpet stage. Irrigate 2 times if rain is short.

Cotton I've been doing 6 years now. Need more potash than grain. About 15 kg N, plough deep before planting. Spray more — bollworm and aphids, 5-6 times in a season.

Cauliflower and chili need lots of nitrogen and water — vegetables eat fertilizer. I use chicken manure plus urea. Watermelon I keep N moderate but more potash for sweetness.

I plough for cotton and vegetables, rotary till for wheat-maize to save time and diesel.
